title: Build an autonomously reproducing cell from defined components

concept.text: The innovation would be to assemble a cell from specified nonliving components that can sustain its own essential machinery and reproduce across generations. Its genome, protein-making machinery, metabolism and surrounding membrane would work together: the cell would take up nutrients, renew its working parts, grow, divide and transmit genetic information to offspring. Autonomy here permits a supplied nutrient environment; it requires the cell to maintain the machinery that turns those nutrients into continued cellular activity.

The defining advance is sustained integration. Copying DNA, producing proteins or dividing a membrane compartment demonstrates important parts of the problem, but those functions must support one another through successive generations. A synthetic genome operating inside an existing recipient cell is a different achievement because the recipient supplies an already functioning cellular system. Similarly, a constructed vesicle that repeatedly receives replacement ribosomes and enzymes has not yet demonstrated the stronger autonomy proposed here.

significance.text: If achieved, this would make a living, reproducing and potentially evolvable cellular system something researchers could construct and vary component by component. Knowing the identity and concentration of the starting components would allow unusually controlled experiments on how inheritance, metabolism, membrane behavior and reproduction depend on one another. Successful construction would directly establish that the specified components and processes are sufficient for cellular reproduction under the demonstrated conditions.

Synthesis: Such a result would not by itself identify a uniquely minimal cell, a universal recipe for life or the historical route by which life first arose. Multiple cellular designs could satisfy the same functional requirements, and a design assembled using sophisticated modern biochemical components would not establish that those components could have formed under early-Earth conditions. Its immediate significance would be experimental control over a sufficient cellular system; broader conclusions would require additional comparisons and evidence.

Biological manufacturing is a possible downstream application. Engineered synthetic cells might eventually produce chemicals, fuels or medicines, but the supplied reporting presents these as future possibilities and explicitly says SpudCells cannot yet perform that manufacturing role. Achieving autonomous reproduction would still leave substantial work on useful output, reliability and operating conditions before such platforms became practical.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a complete reproduction cycle in which the system renews its essential machinery instead of progressively exhausting or diluting the machinery supplied at assembly. The SpudCell preprint makes this distinction concrete: its synthetic cells have very limited metabolism and cannot make ribosomes, while feeder liposomes supply enzymes, protein-making machinery, small molecules and lipids. Repeated cycles supported by those inputs demonstrate substantial functional integration, but leave the machinery-renewal problem unresolved.

Engineering synthesis: Closing that gap requires coordinated production and assembly of the components needed for gene expression, including ribosomes, together with sufficient energy and precursor supply. Genome copying, membrane growth and division must proceed at compatible rates, and offspring must inherit enough genome and working machinery to continue the cycle. These are coupled constraints: making more membrane is insufficient if genetic material or essential components fail to reach viable offspring, and copying a genome is insufficient if its instructions cannot replenish the machinery that reads it.

Division and evolutionary behavior present additional integration barriers. In the supplied SpudCell evidence, the five-generation experiment used mechanical division; a separate experiment linked division to expressed membrane proteins but required externally added division reagents. The reported selection experiment also began with an artificially introduced beneficial promoter variant. These results motivate distinct remaining demonstrations: division sustained by the constructed cell's own processes, and adaptation involving newly arising heritable variation rather than selection only among variants supplied by researchers.

current_state.text: Gaut et al., in the preprint “A Chemically Defined Synthetic Cell Capable Of Growth And Replication,” posted July 2, 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.07.01.735724, report five generations of a synthetic cell cycle combining genetically encoded feeding and growth, DNA replication and mechanical division. This is a reported advance in integrating cellular functions across repeated cycles. The five-generation result should not be interpreted as five generations of autonomous division.

The feeder liposomes in those experiments contain no DNA but replenish enzymes and small molecules needed for the system, including RNA polymerase, the Phi29 DNA-replication enzyme and the PURE protein-synthesis system. They also supply ribosomes and lipids. The authors explicitly identify the inability to make ribosomes and the cells' limited metabolism as remaining limitations. Continued reproduction under this feeding regime therefore does not establish that the cells synthesize and renew all of their essential machinery.

Separately, the preprint reports coupling feeding, DNA replication and division through expressed membrane proteins, with externally supplied streptavidin and antibody linkers used to induce division. This experiment extends the connection between genetic expression and membrane behavior, but must be distinguished from the mechanically divided five-generation series. The reported selection experiment likewise demonstrates a narrower result than spontaneous adaptive evolution: researchers introduced a beneficial promoter variant and then observed selection involving that variant.

These SpudCell findings are unreviewed reported results. According to the supplied review, the retained landing page verifies the paper's identity and posting date, and the retained PDF extracts permit inspection of substantial results and methods. Both PDF extracts nevertheless end during Methods section 21 on page 41; some numerical extraction is damaged, and figures and supplementary data were not visually inspected. This supports describing what the authors report while leaving a full methodological assessment incomplete. The earlier research note's account of a 403 response does not describe the evidence subsequently available to the review.

Tina Hesman Saey's July 17, 2026 Science News report also describes SpudCells' dependence on supplied protein-making machinery and chemical assistance. It provides a separate journalistic account consistent with those limitations, rather than independent experimental replication. The retained article records an August 17 correction, so the supplied review concerns that updated version and does not establish the exact wording of the original July publication.

The earlier research also attributes “A synthetic cell with integrated DNA self-replication and lipid biosynthesis,” DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-69531-9, to Restrepo Sierra et al., with a February 13, 2026 publication date. It describes partial-genome expression, DNA replication and membrane synthesis using supplied PURE machinery. However, the supplied review found only a cookie-access notice in the retained PubMed content, with no article identity, abstract or figure caption available to substantiate those details. The attribution, date and scientific description therefore remain unverified within this record; the access limitation is not evidence that the paper or its reported result is false.

Evidence boundary: The supplied material establishes dated reports and their stated limitations, but contains no completed freshness search establishing the latest field-wide position as of November 1, 2026. It therefore does not justify declaring these the latest results or concluding that no other group had achieved a stronger result by that date. The documented SpudCell experiments themselves do not complete the autonomous-cell milestone defined here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Assemble a cell from an explicitly specified set of nonliving components and show that it takes up supplied nutrients, synthesizes and renews its essential machinery, grows, divides repeatedly and passes its genome to viable offspring. Document the initial components, the environment and every subsequent input so that the contribution of the constructed system can be distinguished from external support. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed autonomy test: Continue reproduction across enough generations, with appropriate measurements of component replacement, to distinguish ongoing synthesis from persistence of initially supplied machinery. No fixed generation count is established by the supplied evidence. Nutrient provision is compatible with this proposal, but continued replenishment of essential enzymes, ribosomes or other cellular machinery would not satisfy its autonomy requirement. The experiment should also show how division is sustained without repeated mechanical intervention or externally supplied division machinery.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed autonomy test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed inheritance and adaptation test: Track genome transmission and reproductive competence across offspring, and demonstrate a heritable functional change under a defined selective condition. Distinguish selection among deliberately introduced variants from adaptation involving newly arising heritable variation. The latter would provide stronger evidence that the constructed system supports evolutionary change beyond the variants chosen at assembly.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed inheritance and adaptation test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: Independent groups should reproduce the central construction and sustained reproduction result, with controls excluding carryover of living cells. Reports should specify nutrient dependence, environmental requirements, duration, generation count and failure conditions. Finite experiments would establish reproduction and adaptation across the tested conditions; they would not establish literal universality, indefinite persistence or independence from every environmental resource.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIO-02, “Demonstrate a plausible chemical transition from nonlife to evolution,” shares the interest in constructing systems capable of inheritance and evolutionary change. BIO-01 asks whether specified components can sustain an autonomous cell; BIO-02 additionally asks whether a chemically plausible route can lead from nonlife to evolution. A successful BIO-01 construction using modern biochemical machinery would not automatically resolve that origin-of-life requirement.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-03, “Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts,” and BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins,” could benefit from a controlled synthetic cellular platform. Such a platform could support direct perturbation experiments with known components, but explaining behavior in one constructed cell would not establish predictive generality across biological contexts or resolve functions throughout natural genomes.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” concerns a predictive model, whereas BIO-01 concerns a physical reproducing system. They could support one another through model-guided construction and experimental tests. BIO-10, “Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale,” supplies a complementary measurement goal: observing molecular processes could help determine whether a constructed cell actually renews its machinery and coordinates reproduction.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” could supply useful catalytic components for synthetic metabolism. BIO-01 would still require those enzymes to function within a coordinated, self-maintaining cellular cycle. BIO-15, “Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body,” overlaps through genome manipulation, but its defining challenge is selective delivery in an organism rather than construction of a reproducing cell from components.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-11, “Reconstruct the major steps in the origin of eukaryotic cells,” and BIO-12, “Explain how biological homochirality could emerge and persist,” address distinct historical and mechanistic questions about life's organization. Constructed cells might become experimental tools for investigating aspects of those questions, but autonomous reproduction alone would not explain eukaryotic origins or the emergence and persistence of molecular handedness.

change_log.change: Preserved BIO-01 and its title while integrating the bottom-up construction goal with the review's sustained machinery-renewal distinction.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent even though individual supporting assertions have different evidence limitations.

change_log.change: Replaced the general claim that the SpudCell preprint was inaccessible with the review's account of substantial retained results and methods, while preserving truncation and inspection limitations.
change_log.reason: The retained evidence supersedes the earlier access account but does not permit a full methodological audit.

change_log.change: Added Gaut et al., the verified July 2, 2026 posting date, and the reported five-generation result; separated mechanical division from the separate chemically assisted division experiment.
change_log.reason: These distinctions preserve supported quantitative detail without implying repeated autonomous division.

change_log.change: Specified replenishment of enzymes, ribosomes and translation machinery, and distinguished introduced-variant selection from newly arising adaptive variation.
change_log.reason: These are central scientific limits on interpreting reproduction and evolution in the reported system.

change_log.change: Retained the attributed Restrepo Sierra result as an explicitly unverified report rather than an established achievement.
change_log.reason: The review's retained PubMed content contains only an access notice; this does not establish the attribution or refute the reported result.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed autonomy criterion to require sustained renewal and exclude continued essential-machinery supplementation.
change_log.reason: Calling such supplementation merely a weaker demonstration was inconsistent with requiring the cell to maintain its own essential machinery.

change_log.change: Integrated limits on sufficiency, minimality, historical origin and manufacturing impact, and added distinct relationships to relevant roster entries.
change_log.reason: The revolutionary significance is conditional and does not imply a universal recipe for life, an origin-of-life reconstruction or immediate commercial capability.

change_log.change: Separated dated evidence from claims about the latest field-wide state and identified the updated Science News article.
change_log.reason: The freshness search record is empty, and the retained reporting includes an August 17 correction.

unresolved_issues: The attributed Restrepo Sierra paper's identity, February 13, 2026 date, DOI association and scientific results remain unverified from the supplied retained content.
The SpudCell evidence is a preprint; the supplied material does not establish independent experimental replication or a later peer-reviewed outcome.
Both retained preprint PDF extracts truncate during Methods section 21 on page 41; damaged numerical extraction and uninspected figures and supplements limit methodological assessment.
The supplied material does not establish the latest field-wide state as of November 1, 2026 or resolve whether later work met stronger autonomy criteria.
The proposed completion criteria leave the necessary generation count and measurements of machinery renewal to experimental design; no validated universal threshold is supplied.
